extracted.intended_audience: Vietnamese and foreign organizations and individuals interacting with Vietnam's intellectual property system (e.g., patent applicants, IP attorneys, rights holders, customs and enforcement agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules (Law No.50/2005/QH11) governing intellectual property in Vietnam, including definitions, conditions for protection, establishment of rights, remedies, enforcement, customs controls, procedural obligations, and terms of protection relevant to patents and other industrial property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters of industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matters of industrial property rights include inventions, industrial designs, layout-designs of semiconductor integrated circuits, trade secrets, marks, trade names and geographical indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of industrial property protections to which the law and registration/protection regimes apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention means a technical solution in form of a product or a process which is intended to solve a problem by application of laws of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory concept of 'invention' that is the subject of patent protection; determines what types of contributions are potentially patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of industrial property rights by registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights to an invention, industrial design, layout-design, mark or geographical indication shall be established on the basis of a decision of the competent state agency on the grant of a protection title according to the registration procedures stipulated in this Law or the recognition of international registration under treaties to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a contracting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent/industrial property rights generally arise via administrative grant (protection title) following prescribed registration/examination procedures; international registrations recognized under treaties may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-known mark established by use
rubrics_metrics.description: For a well-known mark, industrial property rights shall be established on the basis of use process, not subject to any registration procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception for well-known marks: rights may arise through reputation/use rather than registration, important for trademark enforcement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of trade name rights by use
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights to a trade name shall be established on the basis of lawful use thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade name protection depends on demonstrable lawful use in the relevant business domain/area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of trade secret rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights to a trade secret shall be established on the basis of lawful acquirement and confidentiality thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade secret protection requires lawful acquisition and maintenance of confidentiality; disclosure or failure to keep secret undermines protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to repression of unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights to repression of unfair competition shall be established on the basis of competition in business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfair competition remedies are available grounded in competitive behavior, separate from registered IP titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of law hierarchy and treaty precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a treaty to which Vietnam is a contracting party contains provisions different from those of this Law, the provisions of such treaty shall apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International treaty obligations can override national law provisions where inconsistent; relevant for applicants relying on international conventions (e.g., PCT, TRIPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright arises at fixation
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright shall arise at the moment when a work is created and fixed in a certain material form, irrespective of its content, quality, presentation, means of fixation, language and whether or not it has been published or registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that copyright protection is automatic upon fixation; while relevant mostly to copyright, it informs interplay with other rights (e.g., software-related subject matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rights arise at fixation/display
rubrics_metrics.description: Related rights shall arise at the moment when a performance, phonogram, video recording, broadcast or encrypted program-carrying satellite signal is fixed or displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the moment related/performance rights come into existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on exercise of IP rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property right holders shall only exercise their rights within the scope and term of protection provided for in this Law and must neither be prejudicial to the State’s interests, public interests, legitimate rights and interests of other organizations and individuals, nor violate other relevant provisions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights are subject to statutory scope, term and public interest limitations; compulsory restrictions may be applied for defense/security or state/social objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may prohibit/restrict or compel licensing in certain public-interest circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the achievement of defense, security, people’s life-related objectives and other interests of the State and society specified in this Law should be guaranteed, the State may prohibit or restrict the exercise of intellectual property rights by the holders or compel the licensing by the holders of one or several of their rights to other organizations or individuals with appropriate terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits compulsory measures/licensing in emergencies or important public-interest situations; relevant for compulsory licensing or government use.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP fees and charges obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations and individuals shall have to pay fees and/or charges when carrying out the procedures related to intellectual property rights according to the provisions of this Law and other relevant provisions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and rights-holders must budget for statutory fees for filing, registration, maintenance, customs requests, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of protection title
rubrics_metrics.description: A protection title means a document granted by the competent state agency to an organization or individual in order to establish industrial property rights to an invention, industrial design, layout-design, trademark or geographical indication; or rights to a plant variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal document evidencing the administrative grant of IP rights (patents, designs, trademarks, plant variety certificates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting infringement of copyright (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts of infringing upon copyright include: appropriating copyright; impersonating authors; publishing/distributing works without permission; modifying works prejudicial to authors' honor; reproducing works without permission (except specified cases); making derivative works without permission (except specified cases); using works without paying royalties; leasing works without paying royalties; duplicating/distributing/communicating works via networks without permission; deactivating technical protections; deleting/modifying right management information; manufacturing/selling devices intended to bypass protections; making/selling forged-signature works; exporting/importing/distributing copies without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of per se infringing acts that trigger civil/administrative/criminal remedies; useful for assessing whether conduct is infringing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting infringement of related rights (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts of infringing upon related rights include: appropriating related rights; impersonating performers/producers/broadcasters; publishing/producing/distributing fixed performances/phonograms/video recordings/broadcasts without permission; modifying performances prejudicial to performers' honor; copying fixed performances/phonograms/video recordings/broadcasts without permission; disengaging/modifying right management information; deactivating technical protections; publishing/distributing copies when knowing RMI was modified; producing equipment to decode encrypted program-carrying signals; receiving/relaying encoded satellite signals without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists actions that violate performers/producers/broadcasters' exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases of permitted use without permission or payment (copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain uses do not require permission or payment: duplication by authors for scientific research/teaching; reasonable recitation for commentary/illustration without misrepresenting authors' views; recitation in press or broadcasts for informative purpose; recitation in schools for lecturing (non-commercial); reprographic reproduction by libraries for archival/research; performance in mass cultural/communication activities without charge; audiovisual recording for reporting current events or teaching; photographing/televising public-displayed plastic/architectural/photographic/applied-art works for presentation; transcription into Braille; importation of copies for personal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions are subject to non-prejudice to normal exploitation and must indicate authorship/sources where required; some categories (architectural works, plastic works, computer programs) are excluded from certain exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases of use without permission but with payment (copyright/related rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasting organizations using published works in sponsored/advertised/charged broadcasts need not obtain permission but must pay royalties/remunerations; similar provisions apply for use of phonograms/video recordings in commercial broadcasts or activities — payment required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes cases where payment is due even though formal permission is not required (e.g., broadcast licensing regimes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright content — moral and economic rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright consists of moral rights (to title works; to attach real names/pseudonyms and have them acknowledged; to publish or authorize publication; to protect integrity of works) and economic rights (to make derivative works; to display works to the public; to reproduce works; to distribute or import copies; to communicate works by wire/wireless/electronic means; to lease cinematographic works and computer programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the bundle of rights that authors and copyright holders possess and which may be licensed or enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of copyright and related-right protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral rights (certain clauses) protected indefinitely; other moral rights and economic rights generally protected for life of the author plus fifty years after death, or fifty years from first publication/fixation for cinematographic, photographic, dramatic, applied-art, and anonymous works; related rights (performers/producers/broadcasters) protected for fifty years from year following fixation/publication/creation; terms expire at 24:00 on Dec 31 of expiration year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies protection durations for planning exploitation and public-domain entry dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of computer programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program means a set of instructions... Computer programs shall be protected like literary works, irrespective of whether they are expressed in form of source codes or machine codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software is covered under copyright regime rather than patent per se; relevant for overlap issues between patentable subject matter and copyrighted code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright to folklore and required attribution/preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations and individuals using folklore and folk art works of folklore must refer to their sources and preserve their true values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special protection and moral obligations surrounding use of traditional cultural expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of performers, producers and broadcasting organizations (exclusive rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers have moral and economic rights (to be acknowledged; to protect integrity; to fix performances; to reproduce fixed performances; to broadcast unfixed performances; to distribute originals and copies). Producers of phonograms/video recordings have exclusive rights to reproduce and distribute their recordings. Broadcasting organizations have exclusive rights to broadcast/rebroadcast, distribute, fix and reproduce broadcasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies entitlement and economic exploitation channels for related-rights holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where related rights use is permitted without permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication by authors for research/teaching (with listed exceptions), reasonable recitation for informative purpose, provisional copies by broadcasters for broadcasting purpose when they own broadcasting right; uses must not affect normal utilization or prejudice rights of related-rights holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to copyright exceptions but applied to related rights with analogous non-prejudice conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of intellectual property counterfeit goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeit mark goods: goods or their packages bearing marks or signs identical with or indistinguishable from protected marks or geographical indications for those goods without permission. Pirated goods: copies made without the permission of copyright holders or related right holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the types of infringing goods relevant for customs seizure, administrative sanctions, and criminal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of administrative sanctions for IP infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal sanctions: caution; monetary fine. Additional sanctions depending on nature/seriousness: confiscation of counterfeit goods and means used mainly for production/trading of such goods; suspension of business activities in domains where infringements committed for a definite time. Consequence remedies include compelled destruction or distribution or use for non-commercial purposes of counterfeit goods (provided it doesn't affect rights exploitation), compelled transportation out of Vietnam of transit infringing goods or re-export after removal of infringing elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction levels are tied to the value/nature of infringements; monetary fine at least equal to value of detected infringing goods but must not exceed five times such value; Government will specify valuation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal handling of industrial property infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who commit acts of infringing upon intellectual property rights involving elements which constitute a crime shall be examined for penal liability according to the provisions of criminal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious infringements with criminal elements can lead to criminal prosecution in addition to administrative/civil remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventive measures to secure administrative sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Right holders may request preventive measures where acts are likely to cause serious damage to consumers or society; where infringement evidence is likely to be dispersed; or to secure enforcement of sanctioning decisions. Measures include temporary custody of persons; temporary custody of goods, material evidence and means; body search; search of vehicles/places; other administrative preventive measures according to law on handling administrative violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a toolkit for enforcement authorities and claimants to preserve evidence and prevent dissipation before final administrative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional urgent measures applicable to suspected infringing goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional urgent measures that may be applied to goods suspected of infringing intellectual property rights or to raw materials/materials/means of production/trading of such goods include: seizure; distraint; sealing; ban from alteration of original state; ban from movement; ban from ownership transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-ordered provisional measures can be applied at the request of the IP right holder before hearing the party subject to such measures; designed to preserve status quo and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations and security when requesting provisional urgent measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons requesting provisional urgent measures must prove their right to request with documents/evidence and are obliged to pay compensations for damage caused to persons subject to such measures in cases where the latter are found not to have infringed; to secure this obligation the requester must deposit security equal to 20% of the value of the goods subject to the measures or at least VND 20 million, or provide a bank guarantee deed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes evidentiary burden and financial security to deter frivolous or abusive requests for urgent measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation and refund rules for provisional urgent measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Court shall issue decisions canceling provisional urgent measures in specified cases or where the measure debtor proves the application is not well grounded; in case of cancellation the court shall consider refunding the security. Where a request is not well grounded and causes damage, the requester shall pay compensation for the damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects parties subject to provisional measures by providing mechanisms for cancellation and compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to control IP-related imports and/or exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures include suspension of customs procedures for goods suspected of infringing IP rights and inspection/supervision to detect goods showing signs of IP right infringement; suspension is taken at the request of right holders to collect information/evidence so they can request handling of infringing acts or provisional measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs offices have powers to suspend and inspect shipments on right-holder request; important for border enforcement of IP rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations and security for requesting suspension of customs procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters must prove they are IP right holders by producing specified documents/evidence; supply information sufficient to identify suspected goods; file written requests and pay fees; pay damages/expenses incurred to persons subject to control measures if goods are found not infringing; to secure this obligation the requester must deposit security equal to 20% of the goods' value or at least VND 20 million, or provide a bank guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to provisional measures: imposes evidentiary and financial responsibilities on right-holders using customs enforcement tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and duration for suspension of customs procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When requester has fulfilled obligations, customs offices shall issue decisions on suspension. Duration of suspension is 10 working days from issuance, extendable up to 20 working days if requester has justifiable reasons and deposits security. Upon expiration, if requester does not initiate civil suit and customs does not accept administrative handling, customs continue procedures and requester must compensate damages and expenses; remaining security refunded after obligations satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies strict time limits and consequences for inaction by requester to prevent indefinite suspension of trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and supervision notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: When customs detects a goods lot showing signs of infringement and notifies the requester, the requester has three working days from date of notification to request suspension of customs procedures; if requester does not, customs continue carrying out customs procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places a short deadline on right-holders to escalate an inspection to suspension to avoid undue disruption of commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions regarding earlier applications and protection titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed with competent agencies before the effective date of this Law shall continue to be processed according to the legal documents effective at the time of filing; rights and obligations conferred by protection titles granted under previous law continue to be protected under this Law, except grounds for invalidation which remain subject to prior law at time of grant; geographical indications protected under prior decree continue to be protected but from effective date of this Law only protected after registration according to this Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how existing filings and protection titles are handled at transition to the new law—relevant for pending patent applications and rights maintenance.
